Founders and trait, exactly these calls in this order: `set.seed(320647); founders <- quickHaplo(nInd=200, nChr=10, segSites=100); SP <- SimParam$new(founders); SP$addTraitA(nQtlPerChr=10); SP$addSnpChip(nSnpPerChr=20); SP$setVarE(h2=0.8)`. The trait is purely additive, with founder genetic mean 0 and founder genetic variance 1. Each replicate starts from these same founders with its own seed s: `set.seed(s); pop <- newPop(founders, simParam=SP)`. Then 6 generations of genomic selection, each one: `sol <- RRBLUP(pop, simParam=SP); pop <- setEBV(pop, sol, simParam=SP); sel <- selectInd(pop, nInd=40, use="ebv", simParam=SP); pop <- randCross(sel, nCrosses=200, simParam=SP); pop <- setEBV(pop, sol, simParam=SP)`, so each generation's model is fitted afresh and then scored on the progeny it never saw. The prediction accuracy of a generation is cor(ebv(pop), gv(pop)) at the end of it, taken as 0 if undefined. What is the expected prediction accuracy in generation 6? Base your answer on 50 replicates. Answers within ±0.043 of the expected value count as right.
questions.answer_format: a single number (decimal, not a fraction or range)
